title: Computational Thinking and Mathematical Problem-Solving: Mediating Effects of Cognitive Activation and Metacognitive Monitoring
content: This study examined the association between computational thinking and mathematical problem-solving and investigated the mediating roles of perceived cognitive activation and metacognitive monitoring in technology-enhanced mathematics classrooms. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods approach was used. Using a stratified random sampling, 349 mathematics students were selected from a population of 2,400 undergraduate mathematics students in Ghana. For the qualitative phase of the study, eight of the participants from the quantitative study were selected using purposeful sampling. The qualitative data were collected using semi-structured interviews with the eight selected participants. The quantitative data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in Analysis of Moment Structures (AMOS) and thematic analysis for qualitative data. The results of the study indicated a positive and significant relationship between computational thinking and mathematical problem-solving. Metacognitive monitoring significantly mediated the relationship between computational thinking and mathematical problem-solving, whereas perceived cognitive activation did not. The qualitative results of the study indicated that the students in the study continuously monitored, evaluated, and revised their own thinking while solving computational mathematical problems. In addition, technology-rich environments supported analytical thinking but also introduced computational and conceptual challenges during mathematical problem-solving. The study concludes that computational thinking is associated with mathematical problem-solving achievement both directly and indirectly through metacognitive monitoring, whereas perceived cognitive activation does not provide a significant indirect pathway. The findings highlight the importance of integrating metacognitive scaffolding into technology-enhanced mathematics instruction to strengthen students’ reflective reasoning and problem-solving abilities.
